question: What is the main goal of Psychological First Aid (PFA) during a crisis?

options.B: To force survivors to retell their stories
options.D: To reduce distress and foster safety

explanation: You've got this! PFA is simply about offering warm, practical support and making people feel secure, rather than pushing them to process trauma right away. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h1)

question: Why should nurses avoid forcing survivors to retell their traumatic event details during PFA?

options.A: It takes too much time during a busy shift
options.B: It can worsen distress and trigger re-traumatization
options.C: Only doctors are legally allowed to hear trauma stories
options.D: Patients usually forget all details of the accident

explanation: Great thinking! Pressing someone for trauma details too early can overwhelm their coping skills and cause more emotional harm. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h1)

question: Which behavior is a classic sign of hyperarousal in a trauma casualty?
explanation: Spot on! Hyperarousal means the nervous system is in overdrive, showing up as trembling, panic, and jumping at every little sound. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h2)

question: A patient stares blankly and doesn't respond when you speak to them after a crash. What is this reaction called?
explanation: Exactly! Staring blankly and going quiet right after trauma is a classic sign of emotional shock and numbing. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h2)

question: What is a primary sign that a casualty needs immediate psychiatric help?
explanation: Well done! Any talk of self-harm or suicide is a red flag that means the patient needs urgent mental health support. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h3)

question: A patient is screaming, thrashing, and threatening staff in the emergency bay. What should you as a nurse do first?

options.A: Ignore the behavior until physical wounds are dressed
options.B: Scold the patient firmly to restore order
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately for bad behavior
options.D: Prioritize them for safe separation and urgent evaluation

explanation: Safety first! Severe outbursts mean high distress, so keeping everyone safe while getting urgent help is key. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h3)

question: How should you approach a frightened patient during an emergency?

options.A: From behind to quickly restrain them
options.B: By shouting instructions across the room
options.C: Without speaking to avoid startling them
options.D: From the front, speaking in a calm voice

explanation: Always approach from the front so you don't surprise them, and use a soothing voice to help calm their fears. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h4)

question: Which statement is an example of helpful, grounded reassurance during a crisis?

options.A: Stop crying because everything is completely fine
options.B: Nothing bad ever happens in this hospital
options.C: Your family member outside is totally unhurt
options.D: You are safe here now, and we are caring for you

explanation: Perfect! Grounded reassurance focuses on the present reality—letting them know they are safe and cared for right now. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h4)

question: Where should frantic family members arriving at an emergency be directed?

options.A: Outside the hospital gates until things settle
options.B: To the hospital administrative billing office
options.C: Directly into the busy trauma operating theatre
options.D: To a quiet waiting area away from resuscitation zones

explanation: Spot on! Moving families to a calm, quiet space protects them from chaotic sights and helps the team work smoothly. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h5)

question: What is the best approach when breaking tragic news of a death to a family?

options.A: Ask a security guard to pass the message along
options.B: Send a text message to avoid seeing their emotional reaction
options.C: Deliver the news indirectly by joking to ease the tension
options.D: Use clear, simple language without heavy medical jargon

explanation: You got it! Direct, compassionate, and simple communication avoids confusion during a deeply painful moment. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h5)

question: How might young children typically show emotional distress after a disaster?

options.A: By writing detailed incident report logs
options.D: Through clinging behaviors and tummy aches

explanation: Exactly! Kids often express trauma physically through tummy aches, clinginess, or acting younger than their age. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h6)

question: Why are older adults particularly vulnerable during emergency evacuations?

options.A: They always refuse all forms of medical assistance
options.B: They never worry about their personal safety
options.C: They are immune to psychological shock and trauma
options.D: They may suffer disorientation and lose essential medications

explanation: Well reasoned! Older adults can easily get confused in strange places and might miss out on their daily medications during a crisis. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h6)

question: What is your primary role as a nurse when a patient needs mental health support during an emergency?

options.A: Discharging patients before mental health teams arrive
options.B: Handling all psychotherapy sessions without outside help
options.C: Treating severe psychiatric disorders with prescription drugs
options.D: Identifying patients who need specialist care and linking them

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you spot those who need extra help and connect them with the right mental health experts. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h7)

question: Which professional is best to call when a patient expresses severe spiritual distress during a crisis?

options.D: Hospital pastoral or spiritual care leaders

explanation: Great choice! Spiritual leaders are trained to help patients wrestling with deep faith or existential questions during hard times. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h7)

question: What is a common consequence for nurses who handle continuous mass casualty incidents?

options.B: Immediate immunity to all work stress

explanation: So true! Seeing constant suffering without enough rest can drain your emotional energy, leading to burnout. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h8)

question: Why is regular debriefing with colleagues a great self-care strategy for nurses?

options.A: It helps process heavy emotional burdens and share stress
options.B: It replaces the need for sleeping and eating properly
options.C: It is required by law to assign blame for errors
options.D: It guarantees a promotion to hospital management

explanation: Spot on! Talking things through with fellow nurses lightens the emotional load and reminds you that you're never alone. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h8)
